ffmpeg.exe bundled in this directory
=====================================

Source:  https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds
Build:   ffmpeg-n7.1-latest-win64-lgpl-7.1.zip (static, win64, LGPL v2.1+)
Upstream: https://ffmpeg.org

This is the "-lgpl" static build variant, which excludes GPL-only components
(notably libx264/libx265) so it can be redistributed under LGPL terms without
extending SnapDoc's own license. H.264 software encoding uses libopenh264
(Cisco OpenH264, BSD-2-Clause) instead of libx264; hardware encoding uses
h264_nvenc / h264_qsv / h264_amf when the machine actually has a working
encoder for one of them (detected at runtime, falls back to libopenh264
otherwise -- see FfmpegEncoder.DetectBestVideoEncoder).

Used only by VideoEditExporter (the editor's Export button) as the video/
audio encode step -- see that class's doc comment for why (a confirmed,
precisely-measured native memory leak in Media Foundation's IMFSinkWriter
that survived several targeted fixes). Screen *recording* itself
(MfScreenRecorder) is unaffected and still uses Media Foundation directly,
unchanged.

To update: download a newer "-lgpl" (not plain, not "-gpl") build from
https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases, extract bin/ffmpeg.exe, and
replace this file. Keep using an "-lgpl" variant, not "-gpl" -- the GPL
variant bundles libx264/libx265 and would require SnapDoc itself to be
GPL-compatible to redistribute.
